interest: ONI suspicion of Japanese fishermen surveying near the Panama Canal.
overview: Instruction No. 160 (1932) tells the Minister in Costa Rica to investigate reports of Japanese posing as fishermen while surveying the coasts.

people.name: Francis White
people.role: For the Secretary of State (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic instruction directing the American Minister in Costa Rica to discreetly investigate reports of Japanese individuals conducting topographical and coastal surveys disguised as fishermen.
subfiles.from: Francis White (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 160 asks Eberhardt to discreetly check whether Japanese fishermen are really surveyors with scientific instruments.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 160 to Charles C. Eberhardt on Suspected Japanese Coastal Surveys
